chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Husayn ibn Nu'aym said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what they added to the Sacred Mosque regarding prayer within it, so he said: 'Indeed, Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) defined the boundaries of the Mosque between al-Safa and al-Marwah, so the people would perform Hajj from the Mosque to al-Safa.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills in Mecca
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: And al-Marwah, the second hill in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What are the historical boundaries of the Sacred Mosque according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the historical extent of the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), noting that the space between al-Safa and al-Marwah was originally included within its boundaries as established by Ibrahim and Ismail. This context is crucial for understanding the jurisprudential basis for performing prayers within the Sa'i area and highlights the continuity of the Prophet's tradition (Sunnah) in maintaining these sacred spatial definitions during the era of the Imams.
